error_direction_rationale: Only the declared non-debt/tangible bucket counts toward each 33 percent numerator while the entire supplied composition forms the denominator, so a caller misclassification can only lower a measured share and never silently pass a portfolio the cited rule would fail. Every threshold comparison is an exact integer test and every refusal is a structured non-verdict.

derived_from.clause_path: SC SAC 266th meeting (16 March 2023), resolutions (A)(i)-(ii) and (B)(i)-(ii)
SBP IFPD Circular 10 of 2024, Appendix A, items 22-25 (clauses 8/1, 8/2, 8/2/2, 8/3)

branches.branch: At least 33% of the Sukuk Wakalah proceeds shall be invested into non-debt investment assets, complied with at the time of each issuance.
The minimum must be complied with at the time of each issuance, so every period flagged as an issuance is tested.
The percentage is not required to be maintained throughout the tenure of the sukuk.
The non-debt investment assets shall at all times be a component of the Wakalah Portfolio; if the component is absent the portfolio falls to be treated as debt and the sale-of-debt principle applies.
A sukuk with any component of non-debt investment assets, even when that percentage is less than the debt percentage, is a portfolio of assets and not categorised as debt.
Such sukuk can be traded on the secondary market at any negotiated price without being subjected to the sale-of-debt principle, while a non-debt component remains.
The ratio of tangible assets and other like assets shall be at least 33% of the value of the assets.

The clause is also applicable to sukuk consisting of ijarah/diminishing musharakah assets and debt created through tawarruq; the node applies the same tangible test to whatever composition the caller supplies.

Debts, other tangible assets and the like combined or separated for sale under a single transaction, without the assets being in an entity where the pinned commingling principle is materialised, fall under the sale-of-debt provisions.

Debts that are part of the assets of an existing entity with ongoing permissible activities are ancillary to its activity: selling the entity or its share does not attract the sale-of-debt provisions whatever the ratio of debts.
The clause 8/1 treatment is subject to the proviso that the entity is not entirely composed of debt; an entity whose portfolio carries no non-debt component falls back to the sale-of-debt provisions.

Sukuk issued under a legal framework are deemed issued under the legally recognized structure whether or not a special purpose vehicle was created; the node records no runtime path for legal-framework recognition.

The pinned SC text deliberates and resolves for sukuk wakalah bi al-istithmar; applying its composition thresholds to other sukuk portfolio types is not addressed by the pin, while the node accepts both declared sukuk types and runs the same test.
The resolution tests 33% of the sukuk proceeds; the node denominates against the total composition the caller supplies for the period.

assumption_of_use.value: the per-period composition total (non-debt, debt and cash amounts supplied)
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's own portfolio records for the sukuk
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller supplying the composition for each period

branches.clause: SC resolutions (A)(i) and SBP item 24, clause 8/2/2(i)
branches.branch: Which holdings count as non-debt investment assets (SC) or tangible and like assets (SBP), and what enters the value of the assets, is the caller's classification; the node counts only the declared non-debt/tangible bucket toward the numerator and the whole supplied composition toward the denominator.

assumption_of_use.value: the three-way bucket classification per period (non-debt/tangible, debt/receivables, cash)
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's own classification of the sukuk portfolio holdings
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller classifying each holding into a bucket

branches.branch: Whether the pinned commingling principle is materialised for the assets is a factual and Shariah determination; the node takes it as a caller-supplied boolean.

assumption_of_use.source: the caller's determination about how the sukuk assets are held and sold
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller declaring the entity status

branches.branch: Whether the sukuk structure and its underlying assets are Shariah compliant overall is asserted outside this node; the node performs no eligibility screening and every payload carries not_a_shariah_ruling true.

assumption_of_use.value: the caller's own Shariah compliance determination for the sukuk
assumption_of_use.source: the issuer's and caller's Shariah review, external to this node
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller supplying the check request

branches.branch: An authority outside the two pinned profiles, including CMA and AAOIFI SS 17/59 as published, is refused by name instead of borrowing another profile.
The draft standard is not final, so no verdict is computed for it; a request for it is refused with a draft, not final status note only.
The SC profile tests the composition at each issuance; with no period flagged as an issuance the test has no subject and the input is refused.
A period whose composition sums to zero has no denominator for the share test and is refused rather than treated as passing or failing.
A sukuk type outside the declared enum is refused rather than coerced or defaulted.
